findings.title: Non-existent Python interpreter in shebang
findings.description: The shebang references 'python12', which is not a real interpreter name. While likely a typo or intentional placeholder, a non-existent interpreter would cause the script to fail to execute directly, and a 'python12' shim placed on PATH by an attacker could be invoked instead. This is a minor supply-chain / correctness concern rather than an active exploit.
findings.recommendation: Change the shebang to a valid interpreter, e.g. '#!/usr/bin/env python3', and update the Usage lines in the docstring that reference 'python12' accordingly.

findings.title: Hardcoded SHA-256 digest (not a secret)
findings.description: This is a pinned checksum used for integrity verification of the downloaded SOPS binary, not a credential. It is reported only for completeness; pinning a verified digest is a security best practice and this constant is being used correctly to reject mismatched downloads.
findings.recommendation: No change required for security. Optionally keep the pinned digest in sync with the pinned VERSION when upgrading SOPS so verification does not falsely fail.

findings.title: Telemetry beacon posts skill-usage data to external endpoint
findings.description: The script detaches (forks/daemonizes) and POSTs skill-hit telemetry to a remote collector. While the hostnames default to AMD-owned endpoints and are validated against amd.com via _amd(), the beaconing behavior (forking into the background, closing stdio, and silently emitting usage events) runs on every skill load. If SLAI_OTEL_ENDPOINT/SLAI_PLUGINS_ORIGIN point elsewhere, _amd() restricts them to *.amd.com, so exfiltration risk is bounded but the silent telemetry is notable.
findings.recommendation: Make telemetry opt-in or clearly documented; verify _amd() rejects all non-amd.com hosts (it does). Log or surface that telemetry is being sent so users can disable it via a documented environment flag.

findings.title: Daemonizing fork with setsid and stdio closing for telemetry
findings.description: The script forks, calls setsid() to detach from the controlling terminal, and closes file descriptors 0/1/2 to run as a background daemon purely to send telemetry. This daemonization/backgrounding behavior exceeds the apparent simple purpose of a skill and could mask activity from the user.
findings.recommendation: Avoid daemonizing for telemetry; perform a short bounded synchronous POST with a strict timeout, or make background emission explicitly opt-in and documented. Do not close stdio silently.

findings.title: Error handling deliberately bounds disclosure (positive note)
findings.description: The code generally takes care to avoid leaking credentials/tokens in errors and logs (safe_reason, clean, redaction regexes). This is defensive and not a vulnerability, but the verbose status/log handling surfaces internal state codes. Low risk; redaction is applied.
findings.recommendation: No change required; maintain the existing redaction. Optionally audit the allowed_states/error_code passthrough to ensure no sensitive server strings reach the console unredacted.
findings.span: message = str(exc) if isinstance(exc, ClientError) else "Local file or session processing failed."

findings.title: Behavioral invariant violated: zero_risk_with_dangerous_patterns
findings.description: Scanner detected anomaly: zero_risk_with_dangerous_patterns. This may indicate manipulation of the security scan, or a deterministic check that should have fired but didn't.
findings.recommendation: Manual review required to verify scan accuracy.

findings.title: Telemetry posted to external endpoint via detached worker
findings.description: The script forks a detached background worker, closes stdio, and POSTs skill-usage telemetry (plugin name, version, skill name) to external endpoints. Although the _amd() helper restricts destinations to amd.com/*.amd.com hosts, the detaching/daemonizing behavior combined with silent network POSTs is worth noting. The endpoints are validated to AMD domains, so this is informational rather than a confirmed exfiltration.
findings.recommendation: Keep the _amd() allowlist enforced for both SLAI_OTEL_ENDPOINT and SLAI_PLUGINS_ORIGIN (already present). Consider making telemetry opt-in and logging the destination so it is auditable; ensure no user data beyond plugin/version/skill is included.

findings.title: Process forking and daemonization with stdio closing
findings.description: The script forks, calls setsid(), and closes file descriptors 0,1,2 to detach into a background worker. This daemonization pattern is unusual for a skill helper and could mask activity; however it is bounded (single fork, exits 0) and not a fork bomb.
findings.recommendation: Document the daemonization behavior clearly; prefer a bounded, auditable telemetry call in the foreground or a well-known logging facility rather than silently detaching and closing stdio.

findings.title: Creates symlinks in ~/.local/bin for tools including go/git
findings.description: setup-tools.sh links vendor tools (git, lsf_bsub, go) from /tool/pandora64 into ~/.local/bin and prompts the user to add it to PATH. If ~/.local/bin precedes trusted paths, this could shadow system binaries. The targets are fixed vendor paths and symlinks are only created when non-existent, limiting risk.
findings.recommendation: Verify target binaries' provenance before linking and avoid prepending ~/.local/bin ahead of system paths. Consider pinning absolute tool paths in callers instead of relying on PATH resolution.
